subject: MAP: HelixCare performance acceptance criteria & TTFT streaming validation
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixcare.com>; Emma Li <emma.li@helixcare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: HelixCare performance acceptance criteria & TTFT streaming validation

Hi Samir / Emma —

Following our kickoff, I put together a concise MAP item for the performance acceptance criteria and the evaluation plan for TTFT and streaming latency. Goal is to have an agreed runbook and two successful benchmark runs before the canary rollout. High-level items below — I attached a one-page MAP PDF.

Acceptance targets (initial proposal)
- TTFT (first byte/token emitted) for single-chat request (warm KV cache): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms
- Streaming latency (per-chunk emit) observed under sustained chatbot throughput: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 < 200ms
- Concurrency: system should sustain 50 simultaneous interactive sessions with < 10% error rate
- Throughput: steady-state token throughput ≥ 1,200 tokens/sec aggregated across the pool

Evaluation plan overview
1) Environment: use HelixCare dev cluster (us-west-2) with provided service account. We will run two independent benchmark jobs 24 hours apart (same testset) to validate stability.
2) Models & config: run gptj-like baseline and a quantized 8-bit variant (gpt-helix-q8). Use 256-token context, typical chat prompt mix from your testset.
3) Metrics: TTFT per request, streaming chunk latency per emitted chunk, end-to-end latency, throughput (tokens/sec), error rate, GPU utilization. We will capture p50/p95/p99 for each metric.
4) Tooling: Redwood benchmarking harness (k8s job + Prometheus scrape) — we’ll provide the runbook and scripts.

Action items
- HelixCare: confirm dataset, test credentials, and preferred blackout window for canary (Samir)
- Redwood: provide benchmark runbook, orchestration scripts, and a first run report within 48 hours of access
- Both: agree final acceptance thresholds and signoff owner (two signoffs: HelixCare PO + Redwood AE)

Attachments: helixcare_map_v1.pdf (one-pager MAP)

Thanks — will schedule the first orchestrated run once we have credentials.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: HelixCare performance acceptance criteria & TTFT streaming validation

Samir —

Great — thanks for the windows and the sample. A few clarifications and the runbook we’ll follow (attached).

Runbook highlights (see attached benchmark-runbook.md for full steps)
- Warmup: each node will receive 200 synthetic warmup requests to populate KV cache before measurements begin.
- TTFT definition: timestamp delta between request arrival at ingress (server-side receive) and first byte emitted over the stream (first token). We’ll report both server-received-to-first-token and client-observed-first-token measured at the harness.
- Chunk size: streaming granularity is 8 tokens per chunk unless model forces smaller chunks.
- Concurrency profile: ramp to 50 concurrent sessions over 3 minutes, hold for 20 minutes, then ramp down. We’ll also run a 100-concurrency stress run to understand degradation patterns.
- Metric collection: Prometheus + tracing. Push aggregated p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and chunk latency; raw traces for p99 debugging.

What we will deliver after each run
1) Aggregated metrics (CSV + JSON) with p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and streaming chunk latency
2) Representative request logs and traces for top 20 p99 outliers
3) Short interpretation notes and recommended tuning changes (if any)

Attachment: benchmark-runbook.md

I’ll schedule the first run on Thu Mar 26 02:15 PT and post the report here within 12 hours after the run completes.

—Connor

Laura Bennett | Sr. Manager, Solutions
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 06:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: HelixCare performance acceptance criteria & TTFT streaming validation — run 1 results

Samir / Emma —

Run 1 completed (Mar 27 02:15 PT). Summary below (attached CSV has raw sample points):

Environment: HelixCare-project-dev (us-west-2), 4x A100 equiv nodes, model: gpt-helix-q8, context: 256 tokens, hold: 20 minutes at target concurrency 50

Key metrics (aggregated across 20-minute hold)
- TTFT (server-receive -> first token) : p50 = 98ms, p95 = 210ms, p99 = 420ms
- Streaming chunk latency (per 8-token chunk): p50 = 32ms, p95 = 78ms, p99 = 160ms
- Aggregate throughput (tokens/sec observed by harness): 1,310 tokens/sec
- Error rate: 1.2% (mostly transient 429s during initial ramp)
- GPU util: 74% avg, memory headroom intact

Observations
- Warmup reduced TTFT variance; first uncontrolled run (no warmup) had p95 ~350ms.
- p99 skewed by ~12 distinct outlier traces tied to specific long prompts; we will include traces.
- Under a 100-concurrency stress run we saw graceful degradation: p95 increased to ~480ms and error rate to 6.1% beyond the acceptance threshold.

Next steps
- We’ll run the second scheduled repeat (Mar 27 14:15 PT) and post the second-run CSV + interpretation.
- Recommend small batching adjustments and a minor increase to autoscale headroom before canary rollout.

Attachments: benchmark-helixcare-20260327.csv

Raw excerpt (top p99 samples):
- request_id: 8891 | TTFT: 642ms | prompt_len: 420 tokens | note: long-system-context
- request_id: 8923 | TTFT: 598ms | prompt_len: 380 tokens | note: multi-turn history

—Connor

Subject: Re: MAP: HelixCare performance acceptance criteria & TTFT streaming validation — run 1 results

Connor —

Great turnaround and thanks for the clarity. The numbers look good against our initial thresholds; the p99 outliers are expected given a subset of long clinical transcripts. Please include the following in the MAP deliverable before signoff:

1) A one-paragraph explanation of the TTFT definition (server vs client) as you outlined.
2) Top 20 p99 traces attached and a short mitigation plan for long-context requests (prefer token-limited truncation + summary).
3) Proposed autoscale threshold change (we’re comfortable with a small headroom increase).

Assuming the second run confirms stability, HelixCare will sign the MAP and request a canary on Apr 2.

Samir
